Job Description: Shape the future of data governance in one of the Nordic region's leading insurance companies.

Do you thrive at the intersection of technology and governance? Are you equally comfortable discussing access models with data engineers and governance frameworks with business stakeholders?

At Tryg, we're looking for a Data Platform Governance Architect who can bridge the gap between governance ambitions and technical reality, helping us build a scalable, secure, and trusted data platform that enables better decisions across the business.

We are particularly interested in candidates who have helped design, establish, or mature enterprise-scale data platforms and who understand what a well-functioning platform looks like from both a governance and architecture perspective.

About the role | Bridging governance, platform architecture and technology

As our new Data Platform Governance Architect, you will act as the technical bridge between our data governance and data platform teams. Your primary responsibility is to translate governance requirements into clear, actionable technical specifications while ensuring governance stakeholders understand platform capabilities, constraints, and trade-offs.

You will draw on your hands-on experience from data platform architecture, data platform engineering, data management, or governance roles to define robust, implementable governance requirements. You will also help design and implement governance processes and feedback loops. You will work closely with the platform team, which is responsible for implementing the technical solutions.

Your key responsibilities include:

• Defining governance requirements and frameworks for data access, classification, lineage, catalog structures, and tagging taxonomies

• Translating governance, compliance, and security requirements into clear technical specifications and platform controls

• Designing scalable access and operating models, including onboarding, approval workflows, roles, responsibilities, and ownership structures

• Advising on governance capabilities within Databricks, Unity Catalog, and cloud-based identity and access management solutions

• Aligning governance policies with platform implementation and producing governance documentation, access model designs, and process descriptions

• Advising and challenging stakeholders to embed governance into platform processes and enable efficient, governed data product delivery across teams and business domains

You will play a key role in embedding governance into our data platform landscape, working closely with experienced specialists across data, security, architecture, and governance to shape standards and practices that support the long-term strategic use of data throughout the organization. You will help ensure governance and compliance enable scalable data delivery rather than create bottlenecks as platform adoption grows.

About you | Platform architecture mindset and governance credibility

To succeed in this role, you combine strong governance thinking with a solid technical foundation. You understand how modern cloud-based enterprise data platforms are designed, established, and operated because you have helped build, evolve, or govern them in previous roles. You enjoy translating complexity into clarity and can confidently engage with both technical specialists and business stakeholders.

You will be most successful if you:

Must-have qualifications

• Have at least 4 years of experience within data platform architecture, data platform engineering, data governance, data management, or related disciplines, including experience contributing to the design, implementation, or evolution of an enterprise-scale data platform.

• Possess hands-on experience with Databricks and Unity Catalog, including RBAC, governance controls, catalog and schema structures, lineage, classification, tagging, and security capabilities.

• Understand cloud-based identity and access management, including Azure Entra ID, Active Directory, RBAC, ABAC, service principals, and storage permissions, and be able to translate governance requirements into clear, implementable technical specifications.

• Have experience designing and implementing governance models and processes for how data is onboarded, structured, accessed, governed, and delivered across a modern data platform.

• Have experience establishing operating models for data ownership, stewardship, and data product delivery, combined with strong stakeholder management and communication skills across technical and non-technical audiences.

It is an advantage if you

• Have experience from a regulated industry, such as insurance, financial services, or healthcare, and have worked with GDPR, privacy requirements, access governance, or compliance controls within cloud-based data platforms.

• Have experience designing enterprise-wide data classification frameworks, tagging taxonomies, and scalable governance practices, where compliance requirements are embedded into platform capabilities and automated processes.

• Understand modern data architecture and platform automation, including medallion architecture, data products, domain-driven ownership models, infrastructure-as-code, GitLab, Terraform, and CI/CD practices.

• Hold relevant certifications, such as CDMP, DAMA, or Databricks certifications.

You are naturally collaborative, analytical, and pragmatic, with a talent for challenging assumptions and turning complexity into practical solutions. You understand how to balance risk, usability, and business value, embedding governance into the platform to enable trusted data delivery at scale.

About us | Data Strategy & Governance

Tryg is one of Scandinavia’s largest non-life insurance companies, serving more than five million customers across Denmark, Norway, and Sweden. With more than 100 years of history, we continue to evolve and strengthen how we use data to create value for our customers and business.

You will join our Data Strategy & Governance team, part of Tryg’s Data organisation, where strategy and consulting capabilities come together with expertise in data governance, risk, and compliance. We set the strategic direction for analytical data and help our business and data domain teams realise more value from data in an effective, scalable, and compliant way. As part of the Data organisation, you will help shape how data is governed and used across Tryg, connecting data users with trusted, high-quality data and creating the foundation for better analysis, faster decision-making, and stronger business outcomes.

We look forward to hearing from you!

Send your application and CV no later than 8 December 2026. We encourage you not to attach a photo to your CV.

We continuously invite relevant candidates for interviews, so we encourage you to submit your application as soon as possible. Once the right candidate has been identified, the recruitment process will be closed.

If you have questions regarding the position, please contact Jonas Linnebjerg, SVP, Chief Data Officer at jonas.linnebjerg@tryg.dk

We encourage everyone regardless of gender identity, age, background, disability or origin to apply for the position. We are proud to have high employee satisfaction, strong professionalism and equal opportunities to develop your career in the Tryg Group. Tryg is the largest non-life insurance company in Scandinavia with activities in Denmark, Norway and Sweden. Every day we strive – each in our own way – to create peace of mind and affect the lives of most Scandinavians. Read more at www.tryg.com

At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**Job Description

****Key Responsibilities

**

• Support the planning, setup, and execution of global clinical trials, ensuring activities are delivered in accordance with timelines, quality standards, and regulatory requirements.

• Ensure trial oversight by maintaining accurate documentation and participating in inspection readiness activities.

• Collaborate with CROs and internal stakeholders to support site feasibility, selection, activation, and ongoing site management.

• Drive in the oversight of service providers, tracking deliverables, timelines, and quality to ensure alignment with study expectations.

• Support risk identification and mitigation activities, contributing to risk-based quality management throughout the trial lifecycle.

• Drive in managing protocol deviations and trial-level issues, ensuring proper documentation, follow-up, and escalation as needed.

• Support trial data review and performance tracking, contributing to reporting and identification of potential issues.

• Work collaboratively within a global, matrixed team environment, building strong relationships with internal teams, vendors, and investigators.

**Qualifications

**

• Bachelor’s degree in life sciences or related field (Master’s degree preferred).

• 5+ years of experience in clinical trial management within the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry.

• Solid understanding of ICH/GCP regulations and the clinical drug development lifecycle.

• Experience managing global, multi-center trials and working in a complex, matrixed organization.

• Project management and service provider oversight skills.

• Good communication, collaboration, and interpersonal skills.

• Oncology and/or therapeutic area–specific experience is highly desirable.

The proposed gross annual base salary range for this position, in the primary location, based on a full time schedule is:

DKK620.160,00---930.240,00

The final salary offer will depend on several factors, including your skills, qualifications, and experience.

In addition to base salary, this position is eligible to additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

**Benefits

**When you join Genmab, you become a part of a culture that supports your physical, financial, social, and emotional well-being. Our benefits include, but are not limited to:

• Pension

• Health insurance and wellness benefits

• Paid time off

• Employee support programs

Further details on compensation and benefits will be provided during the recruitment process.

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

Advanced Pilot Scientist

Måløv, Denmark

**

Your impact begins here

**Would you like to help ensure that drug products for clinical trials are manufactured to the right quality, at the right time, in close collaboration with manufacturing partners around the world?

As an Advanced Pilot Scientist in Outsourced Production, you will play an important role in connecting our Contract Manufacturing Organisations (CMOs) with Novo Nordisk. You will help ensure that manufacturing activities, documentation and batch reviews are handled efficiently and to the required quality standards, supporting clinical programmes as they move forward.

This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys taking ownership, reviewing documentation, solving problems and getting things done in a GMP-regulated production environment.

**

What you'll bring

**We are looking for someone who combines scientific understanding with a structured and delivery-focused mindset. You may already have a few years of experience from pharmaceutical production, QA or a similar area. We are also open to recent graduates who bring relevant academic knowledge, curiosity and a strong motivation to learn.

To succeed in the role, we imagine that you:

• Hold a relevant academic degree within pharmacy, engineering, science or a similar field.

• Bring experience with or strong knowledge of pharmaceutical production, preferably including aseptic or oral drug product manufacturing.

• Ideally have experience from a GMP-regulated production environment. Previous experience in Quality Assurance (QA) and knowledge of relevant regulatory requirements are also considered advantages.

• Are comfortable working with detailed review of manufacturing and batch documentation, as this is a significant part of the role.

• Work independently and systematically, use KPIs to guide your priorities, and continuously look for opportunities to optimise how work gets done.

• Are curious, eager to learn and able to maintain pace and quality in your delivery.

• You communicate confidently in English, with Danish also preferred.

Previous experience working directly with CMOs or outsourcing activities is an advantage, but it is not a requirement.

**

What you'll do

**Your work will centre on coordinating outsourced pharmaceutical manufacturing and ensuring a strong connection between our external partners and the relevant teams within Novo Nordisk.

You will:

• Take ownership of CMO manufacturing activities and follow these from preparation and production readiness through execution, troubleshooting and batch release.

• Review manufacturing and batch documentation extensively, ensuring quality, completeness and timely follow-up in close collaboration with QA and our external partners.

• Build strong working relationships between Novo Nordisk and CMOs, coordinating expectations, activities and deliverables before, during and after manufacturing.

• Provide technical input to manufacturing processes, facilities and production readiness, drawing on your understanding of pharmaceutical production.

• Support investigations, deviations and troubleshooting, applying structured problem-solving and an optimisation-focused mindset.

• Work with KPIs and agreed deliverables to maintain momentum, identify improvements and ensure timely execution of clinical manufacturing activities.

• As our manufacturing partners are located around the world, the position includes international travel, approximately 1-2 weeks pr. Year.

**Who you'll work with

**You will join Outsourced Production, part of CMC Drug Product Pilots in Måløv. The team consists of 16 colleagues and works alongside our internal oral and aseptic injectable pilot facilities.

We are responsible for outsourced oral and sterile injectable drug product manufacturing for clinical trials across phases 1, 2 and 3. You will therefore collaborate broadly with CMOs, Quality Assurance, CMC colleagues and internal project teams.

The team has low employee turnover, offering continuity and the opportunity to build strong working relationships and deep knowledge over time. At the same time, the work is dynamic, and successful collaboration across organisational and geographical boundaries is central to what we do.

**What you can expect here

**This role offers the opportunity to develop broad experience within outsourced pharmaceutical production while taking real ownership of manufacturing activities and their associated documentation. It is particularly well suited to someone who enjoys execution, review, coordination and continuous optimisation and wants to develop strong expertise in GMP-regulated manufacturing.

You will work in an environment where curiosity and learning are encouraged, but where quality, pace of delivery and independent ownership are equally important.

Salary: For this position, the annual base salary ranges between DKK 570,200 and DKK 838,100, depending on the position level. Placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on your competencies, qualifications, knowledge and relevant experience. The range is based on the supplied compensation information for the role.

The compensation package may include short-term and/or long-term incentive schemes as well as additional employee benefits, depending on job level, geographical location, professional area and relevant market benchmarks.

**

Start now

**If you enjoy being close to pharmaceutical manufacturing, taking ownership of detailed review work and creating strong collaboration between internal teams and external manufacturing partners, this is an opportunity to make an impact on clinical manufacturing from day one.

We are looking for our new colleague to start as soon as possible.

Application deadline: 26 November 2026.

Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

If you would like to know more about the position, please contact Associate Director Mette Uhrenholt Vestergaard at MEVG@novonordisk.com or +45 3079 3068.

You do not need to attach a cover letter to your application, but please include a few sentences in your CV about why you are applying.

As Production Planning Professional, you make sure the plan turns into production that runs. You connect the overall Supply Chain plan with daily execution, turn agreed priorities into realistic, stable schedules and spot risks before they reach the floor. You also drive improvements through data, standardisation and digitalisation. Your work keeps test orders, launches and critical batches moving towards release, so treatments can reach the people who need them.

What you’ll bring

You are structured, proactive and calm when plans change. You take ownership, work well with others and want to make things work better.

• A background in Supply Chain, Production Planning, Operations, Logistics, Engineering, Production, Business or a related field. Relevant practical experience can compensate for formal education.

• A structured, analytical and solution-oriented way of working, with the ability to prioritise and stay calm when plans change.

• Strong ownership and execution focus, including the ability to work independently and make decisions within your agreed area of responsibility.

• Clear communication and the ability to build relationships across functions and contribute to shared results.

• Curiosity and the initiative to start and drive optimisations and development activities without waiting to be asked.

• Comfort working with digital tools and data, and a strong quality and compliance mindset.

• Professional proficiency in Danish and English, written and spoken.

Useful, but not essential:

• A bachelor’s degree.

• Experience from production planning, Supply Chain, manufacturing or logistics.

• Experience with GMP-regulated production, SAP, ERP or MES systems, data and KPI follow-up, or structured problem solving.

• APICS/CPIM certification.

What you’ll do

You are the link between the Supply Chain plan and what happens in production. Your job is to make sure plans can be executed, and to keep improving how that happens.

• Translate agreed priorities into short- and medium-term production plans and detailed schedules.

• Assess feasibility against capacity, materials, maintenance, change-overs and other constraints, and coordinate re-planning when conditions change.

• Make sure production orders and materials are ready for execution, and follow plan versus actual production.

• Support test orders, launches and critical batches towards release.

• Work in planning and production systems such as SAP, OMP and relevant MES systems, and contribute to reliable data and transparency.

• Identify, initiate and drive improvements. Challenge existing ways of working and turn ideas into concrete changes through data, structured problem solving, standardisation and digitalisation.

Who you’ll work with

You will be part of Global Manufacturing & Supply, where colleagues work across the value chain from drug and device development to marketed Novo products, scaling molecules, processes, devices and products for the people who need them. In this role, you work closely with Supply Chain Operational Planning, Production, Warehouse, Quality and other Supply Chain functions. Together you identify risks early, keep communication clear and follow up in time, so plans hold when conditions shift.

The role is based in Kalundborg and involves collaboration across the organisation, with some travel expected between our sites in Værløse and Gentofte. You will join a caring, informal and fun team that values teamwork, social interaction and a good sense of humour, and where you are just as comfortable working independently and taking ownership.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to take ownership and make decisions within your area, and your ideas for better ways of working will be welcomed and acted on. You will grow with your colleagues on the job, build new skills in data and digital tools, and work in a team that supports each other to perform at its best.

For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 499,600 DKK – 734,400 DKK (DK), corresponding to the level of the position.

You will be the trusted partner to our Line of Business, bringing stakeholders on all levels, data and ideas together to keep projects on track and make sure the value is realised. Your work helps Corporate Procurement respond to complex, cross-regional needs with clarity and pace, so Novo can move closer to its purpose of driving change for lasting health.

What you’ll bring

You are an experienced project leader who is comfortable in senior discussions, structures complexity quickly and brings others with you. You will have:

• A Bachelor’s degree in Business, Supply Chain or a related field.

• A minimum of 10 years’ relevant experience.

• Demonstrated experience with consulting toolbox, frameworks and approaches and with working with stakeholders on all levels.

• Experience in large, global technology implementation projects where you have brought the solutions end-to-end to your business stakeholders.

Useful, but not essential:

You will lead projects across Procurement Excellence from first plan to realised value, while keeping stakeholders aligned along the way.

• Plan and execute highly complex technology implementation projects, AI initiatives and similar for Procurement Excellence, coordinating activities, managing resources and tracking progress to deliver on time and on objectives.

• Anchor project outcomes and make sure the value is realised, with clear responsibilities for everyone involved.

• Build and maintain strategic relationships with senior stakeholders, and act as the primary point of contact for the complex and cross-regional needs of business units.

• Lead the alignment of business unit needs and concerns with global strategy.

• Oversee the analysis of complex project data and trends, and drive problem solving that turns insight into better project decisions and new ways of working.

• Communicate project status, developments and key insights to executive leadership, and manage stakeholder expectations so objectives stay aligned.

You will be part of the Transformation Delivery Office within Procurement Excellence in Corporate Procurement.

Your closest partners will be colleagues in IT, Global Business Services (GBS) and Corporate Procurement, as well as business units and other areas across Novo, depending on the project. You will not only work with stakeholders from a variety of functions and locations but also of different levels, ranging from senior management presentations to getting stakeholders and future users of the solutions on board.

You will work across regions and functions, bringing different perspectives together, creating clarity on priorities and helping teams move quickly from plan to delivery.

You will report to Associate Director of the Transformation Delivery Office.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to take ownership of complex projects and to make your voice heard. You will be supported to perform at your best, grow your skills through hands-on experience across Novo’s value chain and relevant learning offerings, and develop others by mentoring less experienced colleagues.

Shape how AI transforms manufacturing and corporate functions by turning strategic ambition into clear, actionable demand that delivers real value.

As AI Demand & Portfolio Manager, you will be the primary Enterprise AI demand-management partner for Global Manufacturing & Supply (GMS) and Corporate Functions, including Quality. You will bridge business priorities and AI delivery, ensuring demand is proactively identified, clearly articulated and aligned to create measurable impact.

What you’ll bring

To succeed in this role, you will bring:

• 7+ years of relevant experience in demand management, portfolio or product management, digital or AI transformation, strategy, business partnering or management consulting in a complex global organisation

• Demonstrated ability to shape ambiguous business needs into clear, outcome-oriented initiatives and mobilise cross-functional teams and senior stakeholders without direct authority

• Practical understanding of the AI, data or digital product lifecycle, including discovery, feasibility, data readiness, responsible AI and risk considerations, delivery, adoption and value measurement

• Proven experience developing value cases, benefits-tracking approaches, KPIs and executive-level portfolio or demand reporting

• A relevant Master’s degree in business, engineering, technology, data, economics or a related field, or equivalent professional experience

• Fluent written and spoken English

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience working with manufacturing and supply-chain environments and/or Corporate Functions. Exposure to both is an advantage

• Experience in life sciences, pharmaceuticals or another regulated industry

What you’ll do

In this role, you will:

• Build proactive engagement with leaders across GMS and Corporate Functions, in collaboration with Enterprise AI Delivery Teams, to identify strategic priorities, operational pain points and emerging AI opportunities while maintaining a complete and transparent view of demand

• Lead discovery and intake sessions that translate ambiguous business needs into concise problem statements and outcome hypotheses, with clear ownership, value definition, success measures, dependencies and readiness criteria

• Orchestrate end-to-end demand alignment by connecting related requests, identifying duplication and reuse opportunities, and routing demand to the right Enterprise AI teams and governance forums

• Convene and influence stakeholders across AI delivery, data, architecture, security, privacy, legal, risk and compliance to drive action, resolve ambiguity and surface trade-offs

• Define value hypotheses, baselines, indicators and follow-up cadences with business owners and AI delivery teams, maintaining visibility of value commitments and challenging gaps

• Provide management and governance with clear demand and value insights, including pipeline coverage, maturity, cycle time, bottlenecks and portfolio balance

• Promote a problem-first, value-led approach to AI demand while encouraging reuse, scalability and cross-domain synergies

Who you’ll work with

You will join the Enterprise AI function within Enterprise IT & Quality, where a growing team is shaping how AI capabilities are identified, governed and scaled across Novo Nordisk.

Working at the intersection of business strategy, AI delivery and portfolio governance, you will collaborate with leaders across GMS and Corporate Functions, Enterprise AI Delivery Teams and colleagues across data, architecture, security, privacy, legal, risk and compliance.

Together, you will connect ambition with execution across some of our most complex domains.

What you can expect here

In Enterprise IT & Quality, you will be part of an area that drives impact across the full Novo Nordisk value chain. We stay close to our stakeholders in the business to understand their needs and help reach millions of people living with serious chronic diseases.

Our focus is on ensuring the highest quality for patients, being a trusted technology leader and operating as an environmentally responsible business.

At Novo Nordisk, you’ll join a global healthcare company with opportunities for continuous learning and career development, alongside benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

Every day, we seek solutions that defeat serious chronic diseases. For more than 100 years, curiosity, determination and a commitment to finding better ways forward have shaped how we work. Here, diverse thinking, shared purpose and mutual respect come together to create lasting change.

As IT and automation engineer, you will keep the equipment behind our medicines running reliably. Working hands-on with PLCs, SCADA/HMI systems and industrial networks, you will troubleshoot TFF systems, lyophilisers, chromatography skids and clean utilities across our development pilot plants and production facilities. Your work keeps this equipment available, compliant and secure, so medicines for clinical trials and worldwide market supply keep moving for people living with serious chronic diseases.

What you’ll bring

Our scope is broad, spanning server infrastructure, automation interfaces, compliance and project delivery. No one is an expert in all of it, and you don’t need to be. A solid foundation in IT/OT infrastructure, a proactive problem-solving mindset and the curiosity to grow into the rest matter as much as ticking every box.

• A technical background in automation, electrical engineering, industrial technology, IT/OT or similar, through education or practical experience.

• Hands-on experience with PLC, SCADA/HMI or automated industrial equipment.

• A good understanding of industrial automation, instrumentation and communication between equipment and control systems.

• Strong practical troubleshooting skills and curiosity about how equipment works.

• The ability to work independently on technical tasks while collaborating with different technical disciplines.

• Good communication skills and fluency in English.

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience with Siemens PLCs, TIA Portal or similar automation platforms.

• Experience with OPC UA, industrial Ethernet or industrial networking.

• Experience with Industrial PCs, Windows-based automation systems or servers.

• Experience from a pharmaceutical, biotech or other regulated production environment.

• Knowledge of GxP, IT/OT system validation or cybersecurity.

What you’ll do

You will work close to the equipment, finding the cause of problems quickly and helping keep systems reliable and operational throughout their lifecycle.

• Troubleshoot PLC-based automation, I/O, instrumentation and equipment interfaces, and support, configure and troubleshoot SCADA/HMI systems.

• Resolve communication issues between PLCs, SCADA/HMI, servers and equipment, using technologies such as OPC UA and industrial Ethernet.

• Investigate equipment failures and identify root causes across automation, hardware, software and communication.

• Support patching, software upgrades, hardware replacement and lifecycle activities, as well as the day-to-day compliance and IT security of the automation and IT/OT components.

• Provide hands-on technical support during installation, commissioning, testing and handover of new or upgraded equipment.

• Maintain technical documentation, support change control and validation activities, and take part in the rotating on-call scheme for critical manufacturing equipment.

Who you’ll work with

You will join CMC IT Operations & Digitalisation, part of Chemistry, Manufacturing & Control (CMC) in Global Manufacturing & Supply. In CMC, we translate research into medicines for clinical trials and market supply worldwide. Our team provides the reliable, compliant and secure IT/OT foundation for the equipment across our development pilot plants and production facilities.

Day to day, you will work closely with equipment owners, IT/OT experts and vendors on support, maintenance, upgrades and new equipment. Bringing these perspectives together helps you get to the root of a problem faster and keep production moving. You will report to Asger Cederberg.

What you can expect here

You will work with a wide range of equipment and technologies, from automation and industrial networks to servers and validation, and you will be encouraged to build new skills across them. We value practical engineering curiosity and a willingness to learn, so you will be supported to grow into the areas that are new to you while contributing your own expertise from day one.

You will be trusted to work independently, make your voice heard and take ownership of technical problems, alongside colleagues who share knowledge and help each other perform at their best.

As IT Operation & Compliance Specialist, you will take technical ownership of the IT/OT equipment and automation platforms that keep our pilot plants and production facilities running reliably. You will set direction on connectivity, integration and validation, and right-size every technical set-up so it is compliant, secure and no more complex than it needs to be. Your decisions help turn research into medicines for clinical trials and market supply, for people living with serious chronic diseases.

What you’ll bring

You are a technical expert who is comfortable bridging IT, automation and validation, and who can make clear decisions on complex topics.

• A relevant Master’s degree in Engineering, Automation, Computer Science, IT or a similar technical field.

• Solid experience with IT/OT equipment, automation or validation in a regulated environment.

• A good understanding of GxP, IT/OT system validation and risk-based validation.

• A strong understanding of integration between PLCs, SCADA/HMI, servers, networks and PCS.

• The ability to handle complex technical topics independently and provide technical direction.

• Strong collaboration skills and fluency in English.

jobs.description:
If you’re energized by quality, validation, and complex Automation and IT projects in pharma engineering, we’d love to hear from you!

**Who We Are

**We are a leading pharma engineering company shaping the future of API pharma engineering globally. Leveraging the expertise of 2,000+ employees across Denmark, India, and the US, we design, build and optimise pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities that are essential to the health and well-being of patients everywhere.

Our success is driven by passion, innovation, and collaboration — with our customers and across our teams and disciplines. If you share our dedication to a noble cause and our passion for API pharma engineering, then NNE is the place for you.

**About The Role

**We are looking for an AIT Quality Engineer to join our AIT Project Quality Management team. In this role, you will be responsible for planning, driving, and delivering validation and quality activities within complex Automation and IT projects in the pharmaceutical and life science industry.

You will work as part of multidisciplinary project teams and act as a trusted advisor on validation strategy, GMP compliance, quality risk management, and project quality execution from project initiation through to handover. The role combines hands-on technical validation expertise with project quality management responsibilities, ensuring that deliverables, quality expectations, timelines, and customer requirements are aligned throughout the project lifecycle.

Location Denmark - Kalundborg

Experience Minimum 5 Years

Department AIT Project Quality Management

**How You Might Spend Your Days

**As an AIT Quality Engineer, you’ll be:

• Leading CQV and validation activities for automation, IT, computerized systems, and equipment interfaces in GMP-regulated projects.

• Developing and reviewing validation documentation, including URS, FS/DS, SVP, IQ/OQ/PQ, risk assessments, test protocols, and summary reports.

• Executing qualification and testing activities while ensuring compliance with GMP requirements, industry standards, and customer expectations.

• Collaborating with customers, suppliers, and project teams throughout FAT, SAT, commissioning, validation, and handover.

• Managing validation risks, deviations, compliance issues, and mitigation actions across projects.

**Who You Are

**We care about who you are as a person. In the end, how you work, and your energy is what impacts the results we achieve as a team. As a person, you are:

• Able to work independently while building strong relationships with stakeholders.

• Comfortable balancing compliance, quality, timelines, and project risks.

• Eager to share knowledge and support the development of colleagues.

• Skilled at communicating complex validation topics in a practical way.

• Motivated by collaboration and delivering high-quality results in project environments.

**What You Bring To The Role

**In all positions, there are some things that are preferred, and others, a bonus. If you do not meet all the qualifications listed below, you are welcome to offer alternative experience that you think would be valuable in this role:

• A B.Sc., M.Sc., or equivalent degree in engineering, IT, life sciences, biotechnology, pharmaceutical sciences, or a related field.

• Experience within CQV, validation, GMP, QA, or project quality management in the pharmaceutical, biotech, or life science industry.

• Hands-on experience preparing and reviewing validation documentation, including URS, FS/DS, SVP, IQ/OQ/PQ, risk assessments, and test protocols.

• Knowledge of GMP, GAMP 5, ISPE guidance, data integrity, quality risk management, and validation lifecycle management.

• Ability to advise customers and project teams on validation strategy, compliance risks, and quality-related decisions.

**Life at NNE

**NNE is short for Novo Nordisk Engineering. And for all of us who work here, NNE means so much more.

At NNE, you become part of a vibrant, project-based environment built on close day-to-day collaboration. The role is therefore primarily on-site, with physical presence at the workplace expected five days a week. Limited flexibility for occasional remote work may be accommodated in line with business needs.

We are, at our core, a people business and, as such, committed to continuously developing our people and the way we work together. We do not expect you to know it all from day one, and we truly believe a great start makes a real difference. We therefore welcome new colleagues with our award-nominated onboarding programme, supported by a range of in-house talent and development initiatives designed to support your long-term growth.

You can read more about the benefits we offer **here .

****Did we spark your curiosity? If you’re ready to join our passion, let’s hear from you.

****Deadline of application is 27th November 2026

**Questions before applying? Send us a quick text to arrange a convenient time to chat. Contact Manager Rebecca Larsen at +45 31 91 88 47.

**Please note:

**

• We only accept applications submitted through our online recruitment system

• You do not need to attach a cover letter, but please include a few sentences about why you are applying in your resume or CV

• We invite to interviews on a running basis.

**Fair hiring:

**At NNE, we are committed to an inclusive recruitment process and equal opportunities for all job applicants. To maintain fairness, we request that you refrain from including a personal photo in your CV.
